document.abstract: The current media landscape shows a constant acceleration in the rate of change of technologies for media consumption and production, with increasing user expectations and proliferation of delivery platforms and formats. Business models need to be easily adaptable to sustain the change and support content creativity and technical innovation, such as a shift from file-based to stream-based workflows. Integrated supply chain processes must be put in place for generating and handling large quantities of video and audio in different formats to suit the requirements of different regulatory environments, regional and cultural audiences, and distribution platforms. Delivering on promises of interoperability, scalability, and agility, service-oriented architectures can be applied to media, as standardized by the AMWA-EBU FIMS project.

authors.bio: Giorgio Dimino is head of the research unit on digital archives and television production at the RAI Radiotelevisione Italiana, Research Centre of Turin. His interests include the application of information technology in the broadcast production chain, the design of modern media archives, and the evaluation of technical quality in video and audio signals. He is chair of the EBU Strategic Programme BeyondHD and co-chair of the FIMS Task Force.
authors.name: Giorgio Dimino

authors.bio: Loic Barbou is founder and managing director at Triskel, with nearly two decades of experience in software design, development, and enterprise architecture. He applies his combined business and technology expertise to lead the design and development of Triskel's award-winning professional services and products. His forward-thinking and innovative concepts are well recognized in the industry. He is currently the chair of the FIMS Technical Board, a global group of vendors and media organizations driving the creation of media standards. Barbou studied computer engineering, at the Universities of Rouen and Lannion.
authors.name: Loic Barbou

authors.bio: Roman Mackiewicz has been leading technology efforts at Bloomberg for the past 16 years, where his focus is on improving product quality and maximizing efficiencies and workflow optimization. During the past decade Mackiewicz has worked with an excellent broadcast and software technology team, leading efforts to build Bloomberg's global broadcast headquarters, ignite creation of a truly tapeless global production system, and drive a business focused vision for media workflow and processing. Mackiewicz has capitalized on the convergence of the media and IT worlds to maximize media process workflows and leverage global relationships in realizing Bloomberg's vision.
authors.name: Roman Mackiewicz

authors.bio: Richard Cartwright is a principle software architect at Quantel where he is developing software-only RESTful services for media production and online delivery. Cartwright has previously worked with the British Broadcasting Corp. (BBC) and Red Bee Media to establish SOA-based systems for media management and interactive services. Currently co-chair of the FIMS activity, he has been involved with FIMS from its inception. Cartwright holds a PhD in computer science from the University of Warwick and is an advocate for applying cutting-edge techniques in software engineering within the media industry.
authors.name: Richard Cartwright

authors.bio: Brad Gilmer is president of Gilmer & Associates, Inc., a management and technology consulting firm, providing business and technical consulting services to the television industry. Gilmer is executive director of the Video Services Forum (VSF), and executive director of the Advanced Media Workflow Association (AMWA). Gilmer is a Fellow of the SMPTE and has been an active participant within SMPTE since 1984. He was previously employed as director of engineering and operations at Turner Broadcasting System, Inc., in Atlanta, where his staff managed technical and operational aspects of Turner Entertainment's television networks worldwide, including TBS, TNT, and Cartoon Network. Gilmer is author of the monthly Computer and Networks column in Broadcast Engineering magazine, editor-in-chief of the “File Interchange Handbook” (Focal Press), a contributor to the NAB Engineering Handbook, and is a frequent presenter at broadcast conventions including SMPTE, VidTrans, NAB, and IBC.
authors.name: Brad Gilmer

authors.bio: John Footen began his work in television 30 years ago. He went to New York University where he received degrees in Film and TV Production as well as computer science. He quickly combined the disciplines and played leadership roles in multiple manufacturing companies in developing products that used computers in media applications such as nonlinear video editing, video servers, and more. During this period, the teams he led received patents and two technical Emmys for their work. Over the past ten years he has moved into systems integration and consulting where he has an opportunity to address many of the real-world workflow issues seen across many types of media companies. Footen has co-chaired SMPTE standards activities in 32NF and currently co-chairs 34CS (Media Systems Control and Services). He has pioneered the use of Service Oriented Architectures (SOA) in media, giving numerous educational talks and articles on the subject and originally co-chairing the Framework for Interoperable Media Services (FIMS) effort by the AMWA and EBU. Footen has authored a book on SOA in Media and is a SMPTE member as well as a Senior Member of IEEE.
authors.name: John Footen

authors.bio: Jean-Pierre Evain joined the EBU's Technology & Innovation Department in 1992 after several years spent in the R&D laboratories of France-Telecom (CCETT) and Deutsche Telekom (FI/FTZ). As principal project manager, he coordinates all EBU technical activities concerning metadata and new production architectures. He is the co-author of several EBU specifications (e.g. EBUCore) and actively promotes the use of semantic web technologies in broadcasting. Evain manages the joint AMWA-EBU FIMS project on service-oriented architecture on behalf of EBU. He represents EBU in many standard groups and industry forums such as the Audio Engineering Society (AES), European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI), International Press Telecommunications Council (IPTC), Motion Picture Experts Group (MPEG), the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), and SMPTE.
authors.name: Jean-Pierre Evain
